svg.text: SQL Basics — SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, JOIN, GROUP BY (T-SQL on SQL Server)
SqlBasicsDemo.cs holds the lesson; every query is a C# string that SqlLab sends to SQL Server. Each box is one Explain*() method — see Flow/0-Overview.svg.
Pick the columns, then filter the rows with
IN, BETWEEN, LIKE — and the NULL trap:
NULL = NULL is not true; IS NULL is.
SELECT TOP 3 … ORDER BY Amount DESC
Without ORDER BY the order is not promised;
TOP keeps the first few rows.
INNER JOIN Accounts a ON a.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
LEFT JOIN … WHERE a.AccountId IS NULL
Glue two tables on a matching column;
LEFT keeps rows with no match.
Many rows in, one row per group out.
The running example — the bank. BankSeed.cs drops and re-creates these three tables on every run (22 rows):
Dana Smith (highlighted) has no Accounts row —
the row that a LEFT JOIN keeps and an INNER JOIN drops.
Program.cs → ILearningTopic → SqlBasicsExample.Explain() checks SqlLab.IsReady(), rebuilds the tables with BankSeed.Recreate(), then calls the six methods above, in this order.
Queries only READ the tables (changing data is Topic 12). The connection string is never in the code: it comes from the BTAL_SQLSERVER environment variable (see SqlLab.cs).
Every method (1–6) gets its own Flow/<N>-<Name>.svg AND Memory/<N>-<Name>.svg — same numbering, so the two folders line up.
